answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. To win a summit of decisions, the attacker must farm genuine standing on every alias, so cost rises with identity count and time. Consider a glacier at the center, a reef resting nearby, and a dune beyond the hills: three anchors, none forged, all earned over time.
